transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-23
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Carlos Ruiz (Redwood SE), Alex Mercer (OrionCloud PSE), Priya Narang (OrionCloud PM), Dale Kim (OrionCloud Marketplace PM)

Auto-generated summary: Align on reference arch and marketplace listing; agree on perf benchmark and security contacts.

[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Maya from Redwood here. Quick roll call?
[00:10] Alex Mercer: Alex here, thanks Maya.
[00:12] Priya Narang: Priya on the line.
[00:14] Dale Kim: Dale here.
[00:17] Carlos Ruiz: Carlos from Redwood, hi all.

[01:05] Maya Patel: Cool. The goal today is fairly narrow — we want to map out a reference architecture for running Redwood inference on OrionCloud marketplace, go over any security/KMS or networking constraints, and surface what we need for the listing itself. If we can leave with a clear owner+due date for the reference diagram and a plan for a quick perf run that would be great.

[01:30] Alex Mercer: That sounds good. From Orion side, our marketplace can host an AMI/container listing, and we have two common deployment models: managed image on our infra or bring-your-own image on customer VPC. We want to understand which mode Redwood prefers and what signals to show in the listing (throughput, latency, supported model sizes).

[02:05] Carlos Ruiz: For reference arch, Redwood supports a hosted API, dedicated pools, and private (VPC/on-prem). For a marketplace listing we usually recommend offering a reference container image that customers can deploy into OrionCloud VPC, and an optional managed listing that Orion can operate for customers who want turn-key. For the container, we need to document GPU requirements, recommended instance types, nvlink/rdma notes, and default config for batching and KV cache.

[02:50] Priya Narang: Question around security — our customers often require KMS integration and audit logs. Does Redwood support customer-managed keys and detailed audit logs for inference?

[03:10] Maya Patel: Yes, we do. Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs. There are a couple of implementation details to validate (key wrapping, rotation process) — we'll need Alex's security contact so we can map to Orion's KMS offerings. Also need to confirm what Orion exposes in the marketplace for SSO and SAML for admin consoles.

[03:45] Alex Mercer: Noted. I'll share the security contact after the call. We have two KMS options depending on region; we'll send the matrix.

[04:10] Dale Kim: For the marketplace listing, we need a short blurb, supported regions, pricing guidance (e.g., per-instance hourly and recommended instance types), and ideally a small benchmark table so customers can see expected throughput/latency. Is Redwood comfortable providing a sample benchmark?

[04:40] Carlos Ruiz: Yes, we can run a quick benchmark. For the listing I'd rather provide a conservative baseline (e.g., 95th pct latency for a 512-token tail, throughput for 16 concurrent connections) and note that performance varies with model and quantization. We can include recommendations: CPU-only not recommended for generation, 1xA10/A30 equivalent for small production, 4xA100-type for high throughput, etc.

[05:20] Priya Narang: We also have marketplace constraints around container size and network egress rules. Do you need any special kernel modules or drivers bundled?

[05:35] Carlos Ruiz: For GPU images we recommend Nvidia drivers and CUDA; if Orion provides a base GPU image we can build on top. For managed listings we can co-manage driver updates, but need to document supported driver versions. No specialized kernel modules beyond nvidia/cuda at first pass, but if customers want weird hardware (e.g., custom inferencing accelerators) we should call that out as unsupported until we test.

[06:10] Maya Patel: On the integration points: 1) reference container image and deployment manifest (terraform/helm) for BYO, 2) optional managed listing run by Orion with Redwood support, 3) marketplace metadata (pricing, supported models, regions, SLAs), and 4) security/KMS integration doc.

[06:40] Alex Mercer: Sounds right. For metadata we also need a short integration test - a smoke check that validates the service starts and responds to a simple /health and /generate call. Can Redwood provide a small test harness?

[06:55] Carlos Ruiz: Absolutely — we'll provide a minimal smoke test script that hits health and a sample generation with a tiny model. We'll include container tags and expected exit codes.

[07:20] Priya Narang: On-rollout: Are there any recommended hard limits we should configure in marketplace (like max concurrent tokens or default batch size) to protect customers from runaway costs?

[07:37] Maya Patel: Good call. We recommend default rate-limit settings and token caps per second for first-run images, and a note directing customers to Redwood billing controls and quotas. We'll share suggested defaults — they vary by instance size.

[08:05] Dale Kim: Regarding billing/pricing guidance, do you typically recommend per-token billing or per-instance hourly with observed throughput? For marketplace listings customers sometimes expect an hourly price for managed instances.

[08:20] Maya Patel: We do both. For managed offerings, per-instance hourly with an SLA works well; for BYO container, giving an expected per-token range plus recommended instance types helps customers estimate costs. We'll provide both templates in the marketplace doc.

[09:00] Alex Mercer: Ok, on the perf benchmark — what model and test should we run to give a representative number?

[09:12] Carlos Ruiz: Suggest running an open LLM we ship in our catalog (quantized if possible) with a 256-512 token generation profile. We'll measure p95 latency and throughput for 8 and 16 concurrent clients. For the initial smoke we can use a small gpt-like model to keep costs low. I'll run on an OrionCloud small GPU instance class (you mentioned A10-equivalent) and share raw logs.

[10:05] Priya Narang: A couple of follow-ons: 1) network egress — if the instance sends telemetry to Redwood for observability, customers need to opt-in; 2) RBAC in console — marketplace buyers will expect role controls.

[10:25] Maya Patel: For telemetry we can default to opt-out. Observability offers like metrics and traces require consent. For RBAC, Redwood Console supports role-based access; we'll include recommended roles for marketplace deployments and default admin roles.

[11:00] Dale Kim: Any potential blockers you see from a devops or infra standpoint?

[11:07] Carlos Ruiz: Biggest potential blocker is driver compat matrix and instance types. Also if customers want a fully managed offering we should align on support boundaries — who does first-line triage.

[11:30] Alex Mercer: For the managed listing we can offer co-managed ops; we should draft an SLA and ops runbook.

[12:00] Maya Patel: Great. Quick timeline proposal: Maya to send reference architecture and terraform/helm snippets by 2026-06-30; Alex to provide security contact and KMS matrix by 2026-06-28; Carlos to run benchmark and share numbers by 2026-07-05; follow-up meeting week of 2026-07-06 to review listing content and initial benchmark.

[12:40] Priya Narang: Works for us. One more minor item — is there a canonical logo/brand asset we should use for the listing?

[12:50] Maya Patel: Yes we'll send brand assets along with the listing blurb.

[13:10] Alex Mercer: I'll also loop in our legal/procurement contact to start on the co-managed terms, if needed.

[51:30] Maya Patel: Ok folks, thanks — recap in chat. We'll share the draft reference arch and the small smoke test, and Carlos will post the benchmark results. Alex will send security contact. Talk soon.
